title: When the Horizon Falls
premise: Jude Lockridge, a riverboat captain who measures life in miles rather than years, inherits more than a map when dying prospector Elias Vane trades it for a promise: deliver his findings to the daughter he abandoned. The map points to the Meridian Star, a salvage wreck sunk in disputed waters holding proof of a fraudulent inheritance that built the empire of shipping magnate Corvus Hale — the man whose fleet now hunts Jude downriver. As tides and the dry season close in, Jude discovers the abandoned daughter is closer than she ever imagined, forcing her to confront the family she fled and the power she never wanted. In the end, Jude beats the fleet by a single tide, sinks the evidence rather than sell it, and chooses the river — and the found family aboard her boat — over the corrupted legacy she could have claimed.
about_author: Lena Fairweather is a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working cargo runs on inland waterways before trading her river boots for a writing desk. Her fiction draws on the rhythms of river towns, where every mile of water carries someone's buried history.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Third-person limited POV on Jude Lockridge as she pilots her aging riverboat through low water, establishing her rule-bound, solitary life and her crew: engineer Tam and cook Marisol. A dying prospector, Elias Vane, stumbles aboard at dusk begging passage. Emotional beat: restless contentment about to crack.

chapters.title: A Map for a Promise
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Vane, feverish and failing, trades a wax-sealed map for one promise: find his daughter, Ada, and give her what's hers. He dies at dawn. Jude finds a second document hidden in the map's backing — names, dates, and the word 'Meridian.' Emotional beat: reluctant obligation hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The crew debates burning the map; rumors spread at the fuel dock that Corvus Hale's salvage fleet is buying information about the Meridian Star. A stranger photographs their boat. Jude refuses to explain herself, straining trust. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by secrecy.

chapters.title: Daughter of the Current
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Following Vane's clues upriver, Jude tracks Ada Vane to a mission school and discovers the girl is barely nineteen, sharp-tongued, and furious at her father's ghost. Ada demands to come along. Emotional beat: guilt meeting defiance; Jude sees her younger self in Ada.

chapters.title: Hale's Men
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At a riverport market, Hale's enforcer, Brannock, offers Jude a fortune for the map and hints he knows her real name — Lockridge, of the founding Lockridges Hale ruined. Ada witnesses Jude lie smoothly for the first time. Emotional beat: admiration shadowed by unease.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. A storm forces them into an oxbow slough where Marisol shares her own story of fleeing a powerful family, drawing out why Jude left hers. The crew begins reading the hidden documents: the Meridian Star carried deeds proving Hale forged his claim to the delta trade routes. Emotional beat: found-family intimacy deepening stakes.

chapters.title: The First Tide Turns
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They reach the first waypoint reef and recover a diver's marker from Vane's earlier expedition — along with signs someone else has been searching recently. Brannock's gunboat shadows them downstream. Emotional beat: the race becomes real; fear sharpening focus.

chapters.title: Dry Season Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam calculates tide windows and falling water levels: they have six usable tides before the channel closes until next year. Ada proves unexpectedly brilliant at navigation, earning grudging respect. Emotional beat: competence forging belonging.

chapters.title: The Name I Buried
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Flashback chapter: Jude's childhood as heir to the Lockridge shipping line, her father's complicity in Hale's fraud, and the night she burned her inheritance papers and walked to the river. Present-day Jude admits the documents implicate her own bloodline too. Emotional beat: shame confronted; identity reframed.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Water
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Brannock boards them under pretense of inspection while Hale's divers probe the second waypoint. Ada hides the map inside the ship's stovepipe. Afterward, Jude and Ada argue — Ada accuses Jude of planning to run again when it gets dangerous. Emotional beat: fracture before reconciliation.

chapters.title: Three Tides Left
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. With time bleeding away, Jude makes a devil's bargain: feed Brannock false coordinates to buy a tide, knowing it endangers another captain who might follow them. Marisol calls it betrayal; Jude calls it survival. Emotional beat: the corruption of necessity beginning in Jude herself.

chapters.title: The Honest Thief
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The ruse works but costs them their fuel cache, sabotaged by a dockside informant — revealed to be the mission school headmaster, paid by Hale. Ada's faith in every adult crumbles; Tam anchors her. Emotional beat: disillusionment met with steadiness.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. On the fourth tide they find the Meridian Star itself, half-buried in silt beneath a collapsed bluff. Diving in near-zero visibility, Jude recovers the sealed strongbox — and finds Vane's final letter admitting he was once Hale's partner in the fraud. Emotional beat: awe curdling into moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Two Tides and a Lie
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada reads her father's letter alone: he didn't abandon her by accident; he sold his share of the fraud to fund his search for redemption and left her deliberately poor to keep Hale uninterested. She says nothing to Jude. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into secrecy.

chapters.title: Brannock's Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Brannock corners them at the narrows with guns and a better offer: the strongbox for their lives, plus Hale's word that Ada will be provided for. Jude nearly accepts — the box could also clear her family's name. Ada overhears. Emotional beat: temptation at its most personal.

chapters.title: Mutiny of the Heart
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The crew fractures: Tam wants to sell, Marisol wants to burn it, Ada wants justice made public. Marisol forces everyone to say aloud what the box means to each of them, and Jude finally confesses her name and lineage. Emotional beat: truth as the only glue that holds.

chapters.title: The Last Tide Begins
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Final tide window opens as Brannock's gunboat closes in. Jude runs the collapsing channel — the run no pilot has survived — using every sandbar trick she knows while Tam coaxes the dying engine past redline. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into mastery; the captain fully arrived.

chapters.title: Wreck of the Meridian
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Brannock rams them at the channel mouth; in the chaos Ada takes the strongbox and threatens to drop it into the flood current unless both sides stand down. Hale arrives by seaplane to see his empire's proof dangling over open water. Emotional beat: the powerless seizing leverage.

chapters.title: What Power Wants
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Confrontation on the sinking deck: Hale offers Jude restoration of the Lockridge name and fortune if she hands over the box quietly. Jude sees her father's reflection in Hale's logic and refuses — then does what no one expects. Emotional beat: identity chosen over inheritance.

chapters.title: Sunk Proofs
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude drops the strongbox into deep water beyond any salvage depth, destroying the evidence that could enrich or exonerate anyone — including herself. Hale's fleet retreats as the dry season wind flattens the channel behind them. Emotional beat: devastating liberation; the promise kept in spirit, not letter.

chapters.title: Ada's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada reveals she memorized the key contents of the documents years-proofed against fire and water — not to blackmail Hale, but to testify to a river commission when she's ready, on her own terms. She forgives her father, and asks to stay aboard as crew. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as choice and voice.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Epilogue on the opening of the next wet season: the boat repaired, the crew expanded by one, Jude piloting toward open delta water. She still measures life in miles, but the miles now have passengers worth carrying. Final image: the horizon ahead, unclaimed. Emotional beat: peace earned, journey continuing.
